caption: Anatomy of a US call sign, using the pool's own example KF1XXX. The prefix is one letter (K, N, or W) or two letters (AA–AL, KA–KZ, NA–NZ, or WA–WZ); the numeral 0–9 is the call district (1 = New England, 6 = California, 0 = the tenth region); the suffix is one to three letters. The sequential call sign system has four groups: Group A for Amateur Extra (1×2, 2×1, and 2×2 starting with A), Group B for Advanced (2×2 starting K, N, or W), Group C for General, Technician, and Technician Plus (1×3, like K1XXX), and Group D for Novice, club, and military recreation stations (2×3 with a K- or W-first prefix). KF1XXX — two-letter prefix, numeral, three-letter suffix — is exactly the Group D format, which is why the pool keys it as the valid Group D call sign for a Technician (T1C05). A Technician may hold Group C or Group D formats.
spoken: the call sign K F 1 X X X broken into its three parts — two-letter prefix, district numeral, three-letter suffix — above a small table of the four call-sign groups A through D, with Group D's 2-by-3 format highlighted as the exam's example
